messages:
alex chen: thinking out loud — our current burst cap (per-region) is blunt. during last week's promo we saw small customers starve while a few heavy tenants used >60% of burst. want to propose a granular surge-protection weighting matrix.

maria gomez: +1. can you sketch the idea? curious how it interacts with reserved capacity and cost buckets.

alex chen: high-level: keep steady-state reservation unchanged. add a soft-weight layer for burst that is per-tenant *and* per-route. each tenant gets a weight score (0-1) computed from SLA tier, recent traffic variability, and cost center tagging. burst allocation multiplies weights by a region multiplier. heavier tenants pay higher cost if they consume above their weighted share.

raj ivanov: hmm do we have telemetry for per-route variability? we need 90/95/99th quantiles of inter-arrival and seq-len to compute fair weights.

sophia lee: yes, trace sampling exists in console. I can export a 30-day histogram for the top 200 tenants. will attach later.

alex chen: prototype simulation command (local):
```bash
./tools/surge-sim --input=top200_hist.json --policy=weight-matrix-v1 --region-multiplier=1.2 --reserve=steady_reserv.json
```
output will be percent of bursts satisfied and estimated extra GPU-hours.

maria gomez: what about network constraints? eu-west had 15% more queueing during that window. if we give more burst weight without considering network headroom we'll just push tail latency up.

alex chen: good point — policy will be region-aware and will cap effective weight by a network_headroom factor (derived from p95 queue depth / capacity). default cap=0.5 for regions currently flagged as congested.

ops-bot: notice: region eu-west-1 flagged CONGESTED at 2026-02-12T11:03Z — historical p95 queue growth +18%.

raj ivanov: cost model question: do we bill burst usage at hosted per-token rates or a surcharge? we need to signal downstream billing and allocate GPU-hour burn to teams.

sophia lee: proposal: two-part charge — nominal per-token like normal, plus a burst surcharge bucket in monthly invoice if tenant exceeds weighted share by >10% for 3 consecutive days. this discourages noisy neighbors.

maria gomez: can we tune the weight calc to favour new customers with PLG usage? we want them to have some slack to try features.

alex chen: yes — add a ramp-up bonus for accounts <30 days with cap at 0.25 of extra weight. also circuit-breaker: if an account triggers repeated headroom violations, fallback to a strict hard cap (no burst) until manual review.

raj ivanov: simulation ask: run three scenarios — baseline (current), soft-weighting only, soft-weighting + billing surcharge. compare satisfied-burst%, extra GPU-hours, and tail-latency impact.

ops-bot: deploy note: creating feature flag eng-platform.surge_weighting.v1 — rollout target: 10% customers in us-west for initial test.

alex chen: action items: sophia export histograms (eta EOD), raj run sims (eta +48h), maria draft billing off-ramp text for CS/legal, i'll put the policy draft in the RFC repo.

maria gomez: thanks. low-risk rollout plan sounds good. :+1:

sophia lee: I'll drop the export here when ready.

raj ivanov: will start sims tomorrow morning and post results in the thread.

alex chen: perfect — aim to have a small A/B by end of next week.
